matchstick.title: V↔X transformation via single stick reposition
matchstick.principle: A V (two diagonal sticks) can become an X (two crossing diagonals) by moving one diagonal stick to the crossing position, and vice‑versa, changing the value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a V or X and a single‑stick move could adjust the value by 5 to help balance the equation.
matchstick.example: Move one diagonal of a V to cross the other, turning V (5) into X (10).

matchstick.title: Check numeric discrepancy to guide stick moves
matchstick.principle: Compute the Arabic values of both sides; the difference tells how much the total must change, guiding which stick move can balance the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after parsing the equation, before considering any stick moves.
matchstick.example: 5 = 7 gives a discrepancy of 2, so a move must change the values by 2.

matchstick.title: Preserve equality sign integrity
matchstick.principle: The equality sign must remain a valid operator after the move; it cannot be turned into an invalid shape or removed.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a stick is taken from or added to '=', ensure the resulting symbol is '=', '-', or '+'.
matchstick.example: Removing one horizontal from '=' yields '-', which is still a valid operator.

matchstick.title: Validate resulting characters after move
matchstick.principle: After relocating a stick, each affected character must still be a recognized Roman numeral or a legal operator; otherwise the move is invalid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After proposing a stick relocation, check both the source and destination symbols for validity.
matchstick.example: Removing the only vertical from an I would leave nothing, so the move is illegal.

matchstick.title: Avoid orientation mismatches
matchstick.principle: Sticks keep their orientation; a vertical stick cannot become diagonal, and a diagonal cannot become vertical or horizontal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When moving a stick, ensure the target location expects the same orientation as the stick being moved.
matchstick.example: A diagonal stick cannot be placed to form an I, which requires a vertical stick.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion only when resulting operator is valid
matchstick.principle: Changing an operator (e.g., '+' to '-') is allowed only if the new symbol is a legal operator (+, -, =) and the original operator remains valid after losing a stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a stick is moved from or to an operator, verify that both the original and new symbols belong to the allowed set.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical from '+' turns it into '-', which is still a valid operator.

matchstick.title: Recompute numeric values after transformation
matchstick.principle: After any stick relocation, recalculate the Arabic values of all numerals and re‑evaluate the arithmetic to confirm the equation holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After finalizing a candidate move, compute the new values to verify equality.
matchstick.example: VI = XVI - X gives 6 = 16 - 10 = 6, which is true.

matchstick.title: Plus‑to‑minus conversion via vertical stick relocation
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; moving the vertical stick away turns it into a minus sign, which remains a valid operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the equation contains a '+' and a vertical stick can be moved elsewhere without breaking other symbols, consider converting '+' to '-'.
matchstick.example: Move the vertical stick from '+' to another numeral; the '+' becomes '-'.

matchstick.title: Dual‑character stick relocation for balancing values
matchstick.principle: A single stick can be moved from one character to another, simultaneously decreasing the source’s value and increasing the target’s value, useful for correcting numeric discrepancies.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric discrepancy equals the net change achievable by moving a stick between two numerals.
matchstick.example: Move a vertical stick from an I (value 1) to create a new I elsewhere; one side gains 1, the other loses 1.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick addition creates extra I (value +1)
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to a location where a new I can be formed creates an extra I, raising the total value by 1 without breaking other symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you have a spare vertical stick and need to increase a side’s value by 1.
matchstick.example: Add a vertical stick after V to form VI, increasing the value from 5 to 6.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats sticks as interchangeable, ignoring that vertical, horizontal, and diagonal sticks are distinct.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always check the orientation of the stick being moved and ensure the target location expects the same orientation.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may think moving a stick from '=' is harmless, forgetting that '=' must stay a valid operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never turn '=' into an invalid shape; if a stick is taken from '=', it must still form a valid operator such as '-' or '+'.

matchstick.description: Leaving an invalid character after move
matchstick.why_it_happens: Removing a stick can leave a numeral or operator with an incomplete shape.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After moving a stick, verify that both the source and destination characters are still valid Roman numerals or operators.

matchstick.description: Changing an operator to an invalid shape
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may convert '+' to a shape that is not '+', '-', or '='.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Only convert operators to other allowed operators (+, -, =) and ensure the resulting shape matches the definition.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes tries random moves without considering the arithmetic difference.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: First compute the numeric values of both sides; use the discrepancy to guide which stick move can balance the equation.
